scope: visible concept discrepancies and separately identified process failures; no model edits

findings.title: Head silhouette is a leaf
findings.concept: A crooked angular crystal with an uneven peak, stepped sides and a broken taper.
findings.current: r12 is a smooth, almost bilateral lens with a clean point and continuous curved-looking sides.
findings.fix: Rebuild the outer profile from the front reference landmarks while retaining one connected crystal and an inset fissure.

findings.title: Head lacks fractured surface construction
findings.concept: Long irregular fracture planes, overlapping angular ledges and local chips break up the head surface.
findings.current: A handful of broad uninterrupted planes wrap seven regular cross-sections.
findings.fix: Sculpt large secondary fracture planes and steps into the same shell before adding small texture cracks.

findings.title: Fissure reads as an inlaid stripe
findings.concept: The violet reveal changes width and direction, with broken uneven lips and locally opened fracture faces.
findings.current: The narrow near-vertical purple ribbon and its bevels run with almost uniform visual rhythm.
findings.fix: Shape an irregular fault path, variable opening and asymmetric bevel depth; keep purple behind the lips and a solid rear wall.

findings.title: Lower head reveal is missing
findings.concept: The lower head has a pronounced broken angular taper and wider exposed violet fracture detail.
findings.current: The leaf closes into a neat dark taper with a small terminating purple strip.
findings.fix: Match the lower fracture silhouette and violet reveal without making two separate head pieces.

findings.title: Head profile is too uniformly slab-like
findings.concept: The side and three-quarter drawings show irregular crystal thickness and changing fracture planes.
findings.current: The current profile has one long blade face and a simple continuous back.
findings.fix: Vary depth and the side planes at the actual reference break points; calibrate the oblique comparison before choosing a thickness change.

findings.title: Head surface has no useful crystal/stone hierarchy
findings.concept: Sharp dark seams, brighter facets, chipped gray/brown faces and violet recess contrast distinguish the head.
findings.current: The same soft cloudy surface covers most of the head, obscuring any small facet variation.
findings.fix: Author the head surface around its fracture planes, with deliberate edge, recess and violet contrast.

findings.title: Broken floating crest architecture is absent
findings.concept: Prominent broken horizontal stone bars form an interrupted arrangement behind and above the upper torso.
findings.current: There is no comparable raised arrangement; a couple of rear shoulder slabs do not supply it.
findings.fix: Build the large broken crest/back bars at their observed heights, lengths and setbacks, as intentional floating pieces.

findings.title: Upper floating stone fragments are missing
findings.concept: Small vertical and oblique stone chunks sit around the raised crest and head.
findings.current: The air around the head is largely empty.
findings.fix: Place varied subordinate stone fragments using both front and side references, after the main crest is correct.

findings.title: Violet crest motes are missing
findings.concept: Several small suspended violet shards punctuate the spaces around the head and upper crest.
findings.current: The remaining crystals are concentrated inside the cage or attached to limbs.
findings.fix: Add the deliberately floating motes outside the head; do not restore the rejected loose slivers inside the head crack.

findings.title: Shoulders remain a few oversized wedges
findings.concept: The mantle is an assembly of interlocking irregular slabs with multiple visible depth layers.
findings.current: Three large cut wedges per side dominate the shoulder shape.
findings.fix: Reorganize the primary mantle into overlapping fractured masses and redistribute existing topology to the visible layered contours.

findings.title: Shoulder chips look like cut shelves
findings.concept: Chips and ledges vary in position, orientation and depth and belong to larger fracture planes.
findings.current: The new long notches read as repeated horizontal slices across otherwise plain blocks.
findings.fix: Replace repeated shelf cuts with individually shaped breaks, corner losses and shorter irregular ledges.

findings.title: Collar-to-mantle transition is too bare
findings.concept: The upper ring is nested into a fuller broken upper torso, with stone around the neck base.
findings.current: A clean exposed bridge/ring spans a large open central region between wedges.
findings.fix: Fit the surrounding thorax masses to the reference while preserving the upper ring and its real connections.

findings.title: Shoulder organization is too repetitive
findings.concept: The reference has unequal plate sizes, overlaps and local orientations.
findings.current: Both sides repeat similar three-piece organization and wedge proportions.
findings.fix: Author corresponding left and right plates individually; preserve overall balance without copying the same local arrangement.

findings.title: Rear mantle layering is not resolved
findings.concept: The side view separates the upper thorax, rear shoulder stones and raised broken crest in depth.
findings.current: The current side reads as coarse stacked blocks, with an abrupt broad dark cut.
findings.fix: Resolve those three depth groups independently; do not use a rear shoulder pancake as the missing crest.

findings.title: Upper cage reads as a rectangular frame
findings.concept: The reference cage is a rounded, organic rib assembly enclosing a substantial core.
findings.current: The upper half is dominated by a nearly flat top and long straight side posts.
findings.fix: Reshape the envelope and individual rib curves into the observed rounder bowl/cage silhouette.

findings.title: Rib flow and density are wrong
findings.concept: Curved, canted and overlapping dark ribs surround the core above and below the thin wrap.
findings.current: Sparse upright rods and a simple converging lower basket expose large uninterrupted openings.
findings.fix: Match the main rib directions, spacing and overlap before adding fine metal detail; do not substitute a bone sternum.

findings.title: Lower cage ends in a schematic point
findings.concept: The lower rib bowl is irregular and rounded around the crystalline interior.
findings.current: Most lower rods terminate in a neat pointed basket.
findings.fix: Distribute lower rib endings and curvature around the reference volume while retaining supported roots.

findings.title: Middle stone wrap is too mechanically regular
findings.concept: The very thin sculpted stone band wraps the cage, with a small V and irregular surface edges.
findings.current: The correct wrap concept is present, but its width, section and polygonal edges are too uniform.
findings.fix: Keep its continuity and small V; individually shape edge breaks and relief rather than replacing it with a front-only plate.

findings.title: Core is a few exposed pyramids
findings.concept: A dense irregular cluster of violet crystalline material fills much of the rib cage.
findings.current: Four large clean spikes are easy to count against empty background.
findings.fix: Rebuild the core into interlocking varied crystalline masses with broken internal planes and smaller subordinate shards.

findings.title: Torso negative space is substantially wrong
findings.concept: Ribs, core and shadow form a dense layered interior with smaller irregular glimpses through it.
findings.current: Large empty windows dominate between the rods and sparse core.
findings.fix: Correct core volume and rib placement together; compare the remaining openings in front and side views.

findings.title: Upper ring and neck structure look generic
findings.concept: A sculpted upper collar is surrounded by fractured stone and dark ribbed neck structure into the head.
findings.current: The ring looks like a plain bar and the neck like a short set of exposed sticks.
findings.fix: Model the visible collar section and neck rib arrangement against the close-up while retaining their supported connections.

findings.title: Pelvic fragments are broad horizontal blocks
findings.concept: The front view shows narrower uneven hanging and hip fragments under the core.
findings.current: Two broad symmetric blocks and a coarse bridging arch dominate the pelvic region.
findings.fix: Rework the fragment proportions and orientations using the front image; preserve intentional floating gaps rather than filling all of them.

findings.title: Upper-leg arch and stance need a landmark fit
findings.concept: The visible thigh tops and knee masses form more distinct vertical groups.
findings.current: The model reads as a wide inverted U of large stones with strongly bowed inner leg contours.
findings.fix: Mark hip, knee and ankle landmarks in the same-facing front/side references and fit those groups before refining small chips.

findings.title: Hands do not hang low enough
findings.concept: The concept hands reach much nearer the foot/ground level.
findings.current: Saved fingertip minima are about 1.20–1.24 m above foot level in the 7 m rest mesh.
findings.fix: Fit shoulder, elbow, wrist and fingertip landmarks; determine the required hand length and limb placement rather than blindly stretching the entire arm.

findings.title: Arms remain repeated large chunks
findings.concept: The arms have long broken longitudinal plate assemblies with distinct overlapping fragments.
findings.current: A sequence of similarly sized diamond/wedge chunks supplies most of each limb.
findings.fix: Individually remodel the upper-arm and forearm assemblies into the observed long plates and smaller interlocking pieces.

findings.title: Elbow and wrist transitions lack convincing construction
findings.concept: Dark joint bands and fractured armor transitions distinguish the articulations.
findings.current: Abrupt black gaps and simple connector rods separate coarse stone blocks.
findings.fix: Build the visible cuffs, overlaps and transition contours within the retained rig; keep the whole seated root sections.

findings.title: Digits are too short and blunt
findings.concept: The hands contain substantial hanging angular stone digits with uneven ends.
findings.current: Three short parallel stubs give a compact mitten-like end.
findings.fix: Remodel the visible digit lengths, offsets and tapered ends from the large three-quarter and front reference.

findings.title: Palm and knuckle fragmentation is missing
findings.concept: The hand mass has deep clefts and layered broken plates around its digits.
findings.current: A simple palm cap meets a few short digit blocks.
findings.fix: Separate the visible palm/knuckle fracture planes and shape their recesses while keeping connected digit roots.

findings.title: Finger spacing and individual gesture are too uniform
findings.concept: Visible digits have unequal spacing, angles and armor termination.
findings.current: Digit parts repeat one spacing and broadly parallel alignment.
findings.fix: Give each visible digit an individual direction and gap; establish exact digit count only from supported views, not an invented thumb.

findings.title: Lower shins extend below the feet
findings.concept: The reference reads as a creature supported by its rock feet.
findings.current: LongFractureLegL2 and R2 extend about 19.6 cm and 18.8 cm below the foot minimum; one small crystal extends 2.8 cm below it.
findings.fix: Establish a standing foot plane, correct armor/shard endpoints relative to it, then normalize height and check a ground-plane render.

findings.title: Knees are not clearly articulated visually
findings.concept: The concept has recognizable knee interruptions and dark joints between upper and lower stone groups.
findings.current: The knee region is lost in a continuous bowed sequence of wedges.
findings.fix: Shape a distinct knee assembly and transition; a retained single leg bone does not prevent the visual joint from being modeled.

findings.title: Shin silhouette and layering are too generic
findings.concept: The lower legs are fractured pillar-like masses with narrow seams, edge fragments and local crystal exposure.
findings.current: A few broad diamond faces and a recent inward notch dominate each shin.
findings.fix: Rebuild the major longitudinal faces, corner fragments and inter-plate gaps before surface noise.

findings.title: Feet are monolithic wedges
findings.concept: Multiple broken toe/foot rocks and dark separations create an irregular planted footprint.
findings.current: Each foot is one simple faceted wedge with a smooth broad front.
findings.fix: Model the visible toe groupings, uneven fronts and heel mass inside the existing foot envelope and budget.

findings.title: Ankle-to-foot transition is crude
findings.concept: The ankle is framed by broken lower-leg plates above a layered foot.
findings.current: A broad step from the shin into the foot reads like a shoe sole/block.
findings.fix: Fit the ankle overlap and foot height with the standing plane visible, retaining the intended joint clearance.

findings.title: Limb crystals look like fins or thin pegs
findings.concept: The reference exposes chunky faceted shards with broken bases and volumetric depth.
findings.current: Many additions read as thin triangular spikes or purple patches on a plain face.
findings.fix: Replace the large visible shards with meaningful prism thickness and internal facet changes; use texture for the smallest chips.

findings.title: Crystal placement is too regular
findings.concept: Crystals emerge through local broken seams, exposed joints and varied fracture openings.
findings.current: A similar isolated shard sits on the front of many successive plates.
findings.fix: Place growths according to actual stone fractures and joint cavities rather than a per-plate repeating rule.

findings.title: Crystal size and grouping lack hierarchy
findings.concept: Large exposures, small subordinate shards and deliberate floating chips coexist.
findings.current: The model has a sparse set of similarly legible solitary spikes.
findings.fix: Design a few reference-led clusters with varied size and direction; distinguish attached growth from intentional motes.

findings.title: Stone reads as blurry marble
findings.concept: The art uses crisp angular surface patches and directional fractured faces.
findings.current: Soft gray/olive clouds cover broad smooth planes.
findings.fix: Remove the cloud-noise appearance; create fracture-aligned face variation and preserve clear large planes at gameplay scale.

findings.title: Color grouping is not controlled
findings.concept: Cool dark stone, warm gray/tan chips and localized ochre/olive patches form deliberate groups.
findings.current: Similar mottling appears over head, shoulder, limb and foot surfaces.
findings.fix: Author regional palettes and weathering masks around actual plates rather than one spatial noise field everywhere.

findings.title: Cracks and edge damage do not follow the modeled slabs
findings.concept: Long faults, chips and smaller veins reinforce the large fragment directions.
findings.current: The generic procedural pattern is independent of individual stone construction.
findings.fix: Align major painted/baked cracks and wear to each remodeled slab and its real bevels.

findings.title: Edge highlights and recess contrast are missing
findings.concept: Bright chipped edges and dark seams separate adjoining layers.
findings.current: Adjacent surfaces blend together under low-contrast texture and broad facets.
findings.fix: Bake or paint edge/recess contrast from deliberate high-detail forms; avoid drawing false seams across unbroken planes.

findings.title: Metal is not sufficiently distinct from stone
findings.concept: Dark corroded metal, warm worn edges and small roughness changes identify the cage.
findings.current: The cage reads as fairly plain gray rods with weak weathered-metal detail.
findings.fix: Author dark metal color/roughness and restrained corrosion within owned maps; verify native material response separately.

findings.title: Violet material lacks internal hierarchy
findings.concept: Deep violet, bright fracture faces, dark occlusion and localized pale highlights suggest crystalline depth.
findings.current: The core and small growths are predominantly flat lavender-purple surfaces.
findings.fix: Use facet-aware violet value variation, local emission and darker bases; do not rely on increasing uniform glow.

findings.title: Important head detail has very little atlas area
findings.concept: The head fissure needs a legible irregular material transition.
findings.current: Its purple floor currently totals only about 32 nominal 512px atlas texels of UV area; this is not 32 pixels per face.
findings.fix: Reallocate texel density and simplify low-value hidden UVs within the current map budget after the head shape is correct.

process_findings.title: Comparison framing is not calibrated
process_findings.current: Different perspective and pose were treated too much like matched orthographic drawings.
process_findings.fix: Use the frontal reference for primary landmarks, the same left-facing side for depth, and label angle-dependent judgments as provisional.

process_findings.title: No standing-plane review caught the grounding defect
process_findings.current: A free-floating preview hid the shins below foot level and gave no contact/shadow cue.
process_findings.fix: Add an audit ground plane at the intended sole level and check rest plus sampled poses without changing the native root convention by guesswork.

process_findings.title: Geometry validity was confused with art progress
process_findings.current: Closed meshes, contact tests, equal counts and many revisions were reported without a sufficiently strict visual rejection step.
process_findings.fix: Keep those checks, but reject obvious silhouette/material mismatches before calling a pass ready; close technical defects without calling them concept matching.

process_findings.title: The run-count estimate had no dependable basis
process_findings.current: The earlier 85% projection was not supported by a stable measured improvement rate, and a fundamental head mistake survived several passes.
process_findings.fix: Withdraw the numerical completion forecast and use this discrepancy list with visible correction evidence and user art review.

limits: Source is painted concept imagery with different poses/perspective; no exact pixel-match or percentage is claimed.
Exact finger/toe counts and unseen rear construction are not established from the supplied views.
Native deformation, collision and live frame cost are not established by this visual audit.
preserve: one connected head with recessed beveled purple fissure; fix its shape without splitting it
continuous upper collar and thin wrapped middle stone band with small V; ribs above and below
native eight-bone hierarchy and seven actions, compact weights and supported full root sections
1792 current triangles, 1800 soft cap and four 512px maps; improve allocation rather than raising the budget
